dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For two real-valued functions x and y on Fin n, this defines their pointwise sum by LocalDef001(x,y)(i) = x(i) + y(i).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the vector storedProduct + correctionProduct whose norm appears on the left-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real-valued function x on Fin n, this returns sqrt(LocalDef003(x)), hence the square root of the sum of the squares of its coordinates.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the Euclidean norm of the pointwise sum on the left and the separate Euclidean norms of storedProduct and correctionProduct on the right.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For x : Fin n -> Real, this is the finite sum over every i in Fin n of x(i)^2.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the squared Euclidean norm used as the radicand in every occurrence of LocalDef002.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite type of natural-number indices i satisfying 0 <= i < n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes the common dimension and coordinate index set of both vectors; when n = 0, the index type is empty.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the heterogeneous addition operation supplied by an HAdd instance.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the binary less-than-or-equal relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With Real.instLE, it makes the target conclusion an inequality in the standard order on the real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Nat is the type of natural numbers, including zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The dimension n is an arbitrary natural number, and the square exponent is represented by the natural number 2.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All vector coordinates, sums, square roots, and both sides of the inequality are exact real quantities.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the addition structure on Real whose operation is ordinary real addition.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the coordinate additions in the pointwise sum and the addition of the two norms on the right.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the less-than-or-equal structure on Real using the standard real ordering.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the target relation as the usual real inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given an addition operation on a type, this constructs homogeneous heterogeneous addition by setting a hAdd b equal to a + b.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures that every HAdd operation on reals in the target is exactly the ordinary addition supplied by Real.instAdd.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.sqrt
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the nonnegative real square-root function, implemented through the nonnegative-real square root after replacing a negative input by zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It converts each sum of coordinate squares into a Euclidean norm. These radicands are nonnegative, so it agrees with the ordinary nonnegative square root.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: This gives Fin n its finite-type structure by enumerating every index from 0 through n - 1 exactly once.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It permits Finset.univ to represent all n coordinate indices in each sum.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite set and a function into an additive commutative monoid, this adds all function values indexed by that set.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It adds all coordinate squares; over an empty index set its value is zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite type, Finset.univ is the finite set containing every element of that type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes each squared-coordinate sum range over every element of Fin n.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the heterogeneous exponentiation operation supplied by an HPow instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied instances, it interprets x(i)^2 as the natural-number power of the real coordinate x(i).

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toNatPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a monoid, this defines exponentiation by natural numbers using the monoid's repeated-product operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For the multiplicative monoid of reals, exponent 2 gives x(i) multiplied by itself.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the value represented by a numeric literal in a type having the corresponding OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the literal 2 used as the exponent.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the additive commutative-monoid structure on the real numbers, with ordinary addition and zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the multiplicative monoid structure on the real numbers, with ordinary multiplication and multiplicative identity 1.

dependency_coverage.name: instHPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a power operation Pow alpha beta, this constructs HPow alpha beta alpha using exactly that operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It connects real exponentiation by natural numbers to the HPow notation used for each coordinate square.

dependency_coverage.meaning: For every natural number k, this gives the natural-number literal k the value k itself.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the exponent literal 2 exactly the natural number 2.

binders: An arbitrary natural number n, implicit in the Lean declaration and permitted to be zero.
An arbitrary function storedProduct : Fin n -> Real.
An arbitrary function correctionProduct : Fin n -> Real.
conclusions: sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of (storedProduct(i) + correctionProduct(i))^2) is at most sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of storedProduct(i)^2) plus sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of correctionProduct(i)^2).
mathematical_definitions: For x,y : Fin n -> Real, their pointwise sum is defined by (x + y)(i) = x(i) + y(i).
For x : Fin n -> Real, define ||x||_2 = sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of x(i)^2).
Fin n is the set of n indices 0,1,...,n-1; when n = 0 it is empty.
All sums, products, additions, comparisons, and square roots are operations on exact real numbers.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite dimension n and every two real vectors storedProduct and correctionProduct of that dimension, the Euclidean norm of their pointwise sum is no greater than the sum of their Euclidean norms: ||storedProduct + correctionProduct||_2 <= ||storedProduct||_2 + ||correctionProduct||_2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: There are no hypotheses restricting either vector or relating storedProduct to correctionProduct; their names impose no mathematical meaning.
The dimension n need not be positive. For n = 0, both functions have empty domain, every sum is 0, and the conclusion reduces to 0 <= 0.
No floating-point representation, rounding operation, computed product, correction algorithm, error model, or accuracy guarantee is encoded.
The proposition concerns only the Euclidean norm arising from the square root of a finite sum of squares.
Real.sqrt truncates negative inputs to zero internally, but every radicand here is a sum of real squares and therefore nonnegative, so this causes no semantic deviation from the ordinary square root.
The statement gives only the non-strict triangle inequality; it does not characterize equality or strictness.
Because the proposition has no premises, there is no risk of implication-based vacuous truth from inconsistent assumptions.
